newsitem.title: CANADA: SEAGRAM Q4 BEVERAGES, ENTERTAINMENT REVS UP.
newsitem.headline: SEAGRAM Q4 BEVERAGES, ENTERTAINMENT REVS UP.

text.p: Seagram Co Ltd said Wednesday that its beverage segment revenues for the fourth quarter ended June 30 rose to $1.77 billion from $1.73 billion for the comparable quarter a year ago.
Revenues for its entertainment segment, meanwhile, rose to $1.57 billion during the latest quarter from $1.43 billion in the quarter a year ago, it said.
For the fourth quarter, Seagram said it posted higher attributed earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA) from operations of $335 million on revenues of $3.0 billion.

It said that, excluding the contribution of Putnam Berkley Group Inc, the publishing operation which was sold last December, revenues increased 8.0 percent and EBITDA was 16 percent higher than the fourth quarter last year.
Total beverage and entertainment operations achieved gains in both attributed revenues and EBITDA, it said.
Edgar Bronfman Jr, Seagram's president and chief executive officer, said each of the company's businesses progressed in both the quarter and full year, despite difficult global market conditions.
He noted that at the beverage segment, the Tropicana Beverage Group had an "excellent year," due in large part to the success of its Pure Premium brand in North America.
Spirits and wine operations also achieved strong results in both periods due to growth in key brands in North America and the ongoing benefits from the group's reengineering efforts, Bronfman said.
At its Universal Studios Inc unit, the music group continued to benefit from investments made in labels and artists during the last two years, he said.

Strong growth at the company's theme parks was driven by the opening of two new attractions a year ago, while two movies -- "The Lost World" and "Liar Liar" -- proved to be outstanding successes, Bronfman said.

Seagram's beverage businesses are engaged principally in the production and marketing of distilled spirits, wines, fruit juices, coolers, beers and mixers throughout more than 150 countries and territories.
Universal Studios, its entertainment unit, produces and distributes motion picture, television and home video products, and recorded music; and operates theme parks and retail stores.
